summary:
Planetary landing site simulation

Bullet Project Concept: The research discusses the importance of space exploration and the careful selection of landing sites on the Moon and Mars.

Bullet Practical Objective: The project focuses on utilizing volcanic regions (such as "Harrat") as potential Earth analogs for lunar and Martian volcanic activity, studying their volcanic rocks and landforms to help researchers prepare for future space exploration missions.
details:
What does it do & how does it work?

This project uses Harrat Khaybar in Saudi Arabia as a high-fidelity terrestrial analog for Martian volcanic terrain (featuring matching domes, craters, cones, and ~600m elevations). It combines three components

3D Terrain Simulator: A web platform using NASA DEM data to test virtual rover paths and landing ellipses.

AI Hazard Detection: Machine learning trained on Harrat Khaybar satellite imagery to classify safe vs. hazardous Mars landing zones. 

Field Expeditions: On-site rover trials and soil data collection with local universities and space agencies. 

Benefits & Intended Impact

It significantly lowers space testing costs and improves landing safety for future planetary missions. Ultimately, it bridges Earth and Mars from Saudi Arabia by turning local geology into a hub for space research. 

Tools, Software & Hardware

Data: NASA Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data, satellite imagery, and ground-truth soil data.

Software: Web-based 3D simulation platforms and Machine Learning models. 

Hardware: Planetary rovers for physical field testing. 

Creativity & Factors Considered

Instead of relying solely on synthetic maps, we creatively transform a real local landmark into a virtual-to-physical Martian lab. Our team prioritized geological accuracy (~600m volcanic structures), local cost-efficiency, and practical rover navigation safety.
